name: stri_startswith
title: Determine if the Start or End of a String Matches a Pattern

origin.description: Report whether each string starts with a fixed, collation, or character-class pattern.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: fixed, coll, charclass
arguments.text: One of fixed, coll, or charclass. Exactly one must be supplied. There is no regex argument. NULL is a supplied empty pattern. A missing argument is not supplied.
Further arguments forwarded to the chosen mode function, including settings merged into opts_fixed or opts_collator.

origin.details: Exactly one of fixed, coll, and charclass must be supplied. There is no regex argument. An explicit NULL is supplied and searches with an empty pattern. Omitting every pattern argument is an error, and so is supplying two. Arguments in ... are passed to the chosen function. A name that follows ... is not partially matched. from is forwarded. Indexes are 1-based, and a negative index counts from the end.
origin.example:
result <- stri_startswith(c("a1", "b3"), fixed = "a")
shown <- paste(ifelse(result, "TRUE", "FALSE"), collapse = ", ")
cat(paste0('stri_startswith(c("a1", "b3"), fixed = "a") returns ', shown, '.\n'))

translation.description: Report whether each string starts with a fixed, collation, or character-class pattern.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: fixed, coll, charclass
arguments.text: One of fixed, coll, or charclass. Exactly one must be supplied. There is no regex argument. None is a supplied empty pattern. Omitting the argument is a different state.
Further keywords forwarded to the chosen mode function. The mode functions already accept those opts_* settings.

translation.details: Exactly one of fixed, coll, and charclass must be supplied. There is no regex argument, and passing regex does not select an engine. An omitted pattern argument is a private sentinel, and None is an explicit NULL passed on as an empty list. Extra keywords, including case_insensitive and strength, are forwarded. from_ is R's from, because from is not a Python parameter name. A positional from index still binds.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA. An empty pattern argument returns an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.dispatch import stri_startswith
result = stri_startswith(["a1", "b3"], fixed="a")
shown = ", ".join("TRUE" if item else "FALSE" for item in result)
print(f'stri_startswith(["a1", "b3"], fixed="a") returns {shown}.')
